getting-started-talking-to-guard.speaker: Guard
getting-started-talking-to-guard.text: Oh, it's terrible! Lord Sinclair has been murdered and we don't have any clues as to who or why. We're totally baffled!

getting-started-talking-to-guard.speaker: Guard
getting-started-talking-to-guard.text: If you can help us we will be very grateful.

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Sure, I'll help!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Thanks a lot!

steps.player: What should I be doing to help?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Look around and investigate who might be responsible. The Sarge said every murder leaves clues to who done it, but frankly we're out of our depth here.

options.text: No.

steps.player: You should do your own dirty work.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Get lost then, this is private property! ...Unless you'd like to be taken in for questioning yourself?

options.text: What should I be doing to help again?

steps.player: What should I be doing to help?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Look around and investigate who might be responsible. The Sarge said every murder leaves clues to who done it, but frankly we're out of our depth here.

options.text: How did Lord Sinclair die?

steps.player: How did Lord Sinclair die?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well, it's all very mysterious. Mary, the maid, found the body in the study next to his bedroom on the east wing of the ground floor.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: The door was found locked from the inside, and he seemed to have been stabbed, but there was an odd smell in the room. Frankly, I'm stumped.

options.text: I know who did it!

steps.player: I know who did it!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Really? That was quick work! Who?

options.text: It was an intruder!

steps.player: It was an intruder!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: That's what we were thinking too. That someone broke in to steal something, was discovered by Lord Sinclair, stabbed him and ran.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: It's odd that apparently nothing was stolen though... Find out something has been stolen,

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: and the case is closed, but the murdered man was a friend of the King, and it's more than my job's worth not to investigate fully.

options.text: The butler did it!

steps.player: The butler did it!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I hope you have proof to that effect. We have to arrest someone for this and it seems to me that only the actual murderer would gain by falsely accusing someone.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Although having said that the butler is kind of shifty looking...

options.text: It was one of the servants!

steps.player: It was one of the servants!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh really? Which one?

options.text: It was one of the women...

steps.player: It was one of the women

options.text: It was SO obviously Louisa the cook.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Great work. Show me the evidence, and we'll take them to the dungeons.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: You DO have evidence of their crime, right?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Tch. You wouldn't last a day in the guards with sloppy thinking like that. Come see me when you have some proof of your accusations.

options.text: It MUST have been Mary the maid.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Great work. Show me the evidence, and we'll take them to the dungeons.

options.text: You MUST know it was Stanford The Gardener...

steps.speaker: Guard

options.text: Where were you when the murder happened?

options.text: Do you recognise this thread?

steps.text: You show him the thread you found on the study window

options.text: Where were you when the murder happened?

options.text: Who do you think was responsible?

steps.text: I don't know.

options.text: Where were you when the murder happened?

options.text: Who do you think is responsible?

steps.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
steps.text: I saw him arguing with Lord Sinclair about some missing silverware from the Kitchen. It was a very heated argument.

options.text: Where were you at the time of the murder?

steps.player: Where were you at the time of the murder?

steps.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
steps.text: Me? I was sound asleep here in the servants Quarters. It's very hard work as a handyman around here, There's always something to do!

options.text: Did you hear any suspicious noises at all?

steps.player: Did you hear any suspicious noises at all?

steps.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
steps.text: Hmmm..... No, I didn't, but I sleep very soundly at night.

steps.player: So you didn't hear any sounds of a struggle or any barking from the guard dog next to his study window?

steps.speaker: Donovan the Family Handyman
steps.text: Now you mention it, no. It is odd I didn't hear anything like that. But I do sleep very soundly as I said and wouldn't necessarily have heard it if there was any such noise.

questioning-the-inhabitants-talking-to-g.player: I'm investigating the murder up at the Sinclair place.

questioning-the-inhabitants-talking-to-g.speaker: Gossip
questioning-the-inhabitants-talking-to-g.text: Murder is it? Well, I'm not really surprised...

options.text: What can you tell me about the Sinclairs?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Sinclairs?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Well, what do you want to know?

options.text: Tell me about Lord Sinclair.

steps.player: Tell me about Lord Sinclair.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Old Lord Sinclair was a great man with a lot of respect in these parts. More than his worthless children have anyway.

steps.player: His children? They have something to gain by his death?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Yes. You could say that. Not that I'm one to gossip.

options.text: Why do the Sinclairs live so far from town?

steps.player: Why do the Sinclairs live so far from town?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Well, they used to live in the big castle, but old Lord Sinclair gave it up so that those strange knights could live there instead. So the king built him a new house to the North.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: It's more cramped than his old place, but he seemed to like it. His children were furious at him for doing it though!

options.text: What can you tell me about his sons?

steps.player: What can you tell me about his sons?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: His sons eh? They all have their own skeletons in their cupboards. You'll have to be more specific. Who are you interested in exactly?

options.text: Tell me about Bob.

steps.player: Tell me about Bob.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Bob is an odd character indeed... I'm not one to gossip, but I heard Bob is addicted to Tea. He can't make

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: it through the day without having at least 20 cups!

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: You might not think that's such a big thing, but he has spent thousands of gold to feed his habit!

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: At one point he stole a lot of silverware from the kitchen and pawned it just so he could afford to buy his daily tea allowance.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: If his father ever found out, he would be in so much trouble... he might even get disowned!

options.text: Tell me about David.

steps.player: Tell me about David.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: David... oh David... not many people know this, but David really has an anger problem. He's always screaming and shouting

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: at the household servants when he's angry, and they live in a state of fear, always walking on eggshells around him, but none of them have the courage

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: to talk to his father about his behaviour. If they did, Lord Sinclair would almost certainly

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: kick him out of the house, as some of the servants have been there longer than he has, and he definitely has no right to treat them like he does... but I'm not one to gossip about people.

options.text: Tell me about Frank.

steps.player: Tell me about Frank.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: I'm not one to talk ill of people behind their back, but Frank is a real piece of work. He is an absolutely terrible gambler... he can't pass 2 dogs in the street without putting a bet on which one will bark first!

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: He has already squandered all of his allowance, and I heard he had stolen a number of paintings of his fathers to sell to try and cover his debts, but he still owes a lot of

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: people a lot of money. If his father ever found out, he would stop his income, and then he would be in serious trouble!

options.text: What can you tell me about his daughters?

steps.player: What can you tell me about his daughters?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: His daughters eh? They're all nasty pieces of work. which of them specifically did you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about Anna.

steps.player: Tell me about Anna.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Anna... ah yes... Anna has 2 great loves:

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Sewing and gardening. But one thing she has kept secret is that she once had an affair with Stanford the gardener, and tried to get him fired when they broke up,

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: by killing all of the flowers in the garden. If her father ever found out she had done that he would be so furious he would probably disown her.

options.text: Tell me about Carol.

steps.player: Tell me about Carol.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Oh Carol... she is such a fool. You didn't hear this from me, but I heard a while ago she was conned out of a lot of money by a travelling salesman who sold her a box full

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: of beans by telling her they were magic. But they weren't. She sold some rare books from the library to cover her debts, but

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: her father would be incredibly annoyed if he ever found out - he might even throw her out of the house!

options.text: Tell me about Elizabeth.

steps.player: Tell me about Elizabeth.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Elizabeth? Elizabeth has a strange problem... She cannot help herself, but is always stealing small objects - it's pretty sad that she is rich enough to afford to buy things, but would rather steal them instead.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Now, I don't want to spread stories, but I heard she even stole a silver needle from her father that had great sentimental value for him.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: He was devastated when it was lost, and cried for a week thinking he had lost it!

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: If he ever found out that it was her who had stolen it he would go absolutely mental, maybe even disowning her!

options.text: Who do you think was responsible?

steps.player: Who do you think was responsible?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Well, I guess it could have been an intruder, but with that big guard dog of theirs I seriously doubt it. I suspect it was someone closer to home...

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Especially as I heard that the poison salesman in the Seers' village made a big sale to one of the family the other day.

options.text: I think the butler did it.

steps.player: I think the butler did it.

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: And I think you've been reading too many cheap detective novels. Hobbes is kind of uptight, but his loyalty to old Lord Sinclair is beyond question.

options.text: I am so confused about who did it.

steps.player: I am so confused about who did it...
Think you could give me any hints?

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: Well, I don't know if it's related, but I heard from that Poison Salesman in town that he sold some poison to one of the Sinclair family

steps.speaker: Gossip
steps.text: the other day. I don't think he has any stock left now though...

questioning-the-inhabitants-talking-to-h.player: I'm here to help the guards with their investigation.

options.text: Who do you think is responsible?

steps.player: Who do you think is responsible?

steps.speaker: Hobbes
steps.text: Well, in my considered opinion it must be David. The man is nothing more than a bully And I happen to know that poor Lord Sinclair and David had a massive argument in the living

steps.speaker: Hobbes
steps.text: room about the way he treats the staff, the other day. I did not intend to overhear their conversation, but they were shouting so loudly I could not help but Overhear it. David definitely used the words

steps.speaker: Hobbes
steps.text: 'I am going to kill you!' as well. I think he should be the prime suspect. He has a nasty temper that one.

steps.text: I was assisting the cook with the evening meal. I gave Mary His Lordships' dinner, and sent her to take it to him, then heard the scream as she found the body.

steps.text: No, I definitely didn't hear anything like that.

steps.speaker: Hobbes
steps.text: You know, now you come to mention it I don't believe I did. I suppose that is Proof enough that it could not have been an intruder who is responsible.

steps.text: You have our gratitude, and I'm sure the rest of the family's as well, in helping to apprehend the murderer. I'll just take the evidence from you now.
You hand over all the evidence.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Please accept this reward from the family!
Congratulations! Quest complete!
